goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
goldens.reasoning: G1 is about float: left being mixed with flexbox, and about removing the panel's float, which breaks the noscript header layout. C4 is about leftover clearfix pseudo-elements in a flex container. That is related but is not the same issue, and no other candidate covers the float or panel problem.

goldens.comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
goldens.reasoning: C1 identifies the same issue: -ms-align-items is not a valid property, and the correct one is -ms-flex-align.

goldens.comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
goldens.reasoning: C2 identifies the same issue: the legacy box-ordinal-group properties are 1-based, so passing $val directly gives the wrong order.

candidates: `-ms-align-items` on line 121 is not a valid CSS property (the correct `-ms-flex-align` is already on line 120, making this dead code)

The `order` mixin passes `$val` directly to `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group`, but these legacy properties use 1-based indexing while CSS `order` is 0-based — the mixin should pass `$val + 1` for correct behavior

Mobile layout regression: The padding on `.small-action-desc` changed from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` to `0 1.5%`, but `mobile/topic-post.scss:521` still has `margin-left: -40px` on `.custom-message`. That negative margin was designed to offset the old ~64px left padding; with only ~4.8px of padding on a 320px mobile viewport, the custom-message now overflows ~35px past the left edge of its container

`.contents` in header.hbs still has the `clearfix` class, whose `::before`/`::after` pseudo-elements become unnecessary flex items when the container is `display: flex` — the `clear: both` on `::after` is a no-op in flex context

`@include order(2)` on `.extra-info-wrapper` (topic.scss:29) is dead CSS because `.extra-info-wrapper` is a grandchild of the flex container (Ember wraps `header-extra-info` in a `div.ember-view`), and `order` only applies to direct children
